slides.title: 3 ways to calm your body in 5 minutes
Bare feet on the ground
slides.body: Stand on grass, sand or soil. Notice the temperature, the texture, your breath. Five minutes is enough to start.

slides.title: Morning light in your eyes
slides.body: Step outside before 10 am, no sunglasses. Morning light helps set your sleep rhythm for that night.

slides.title: Say it out loud to someone
slides.body: Naming what you feel to a calm listener settles the body faster than thinking it through alone.

caption:
Your nervous system needs a reset, not a pep talk. 🌿

Three small things that help, no equipment needed. The Nest app has timers for the first two and keeps your streak, all on your own phone.

And for the third, we're a call away. Link in bio.

myth: If you're not in therapy, your feelings must not be serious.
truth: Not every hard season needs a diagnosis. Sometimes you need a calm person to think out loud with, today, not in six weeks.
caption:
Therapy is wonderful. It's also not the only kind of support.

We're not therapists and we're not a crisis line. We're real people who listen, reflect back what we hear, and help you find one next step. Calls are $75, or $50 for Nest members.

text: Mercury is retrograde, and every old conversation is knocking at the door.

text: Your feelings aren't overreactions. They make sense given what you've been through.
caption: You don't need to justify how you feel. You need space to feel it. 🌿

slides.title: Burnout doesn't always look like falling apart
It can look like flat
slides.body: Not sad, not happy. Just going through the motions.

slides.title: It can look like irritable
slides.body: Small things land hard. You're short with people you love.

slides.title: It can look like numb
slides.body: The things you used to care about don't reach you. That's depletion, not laziness.

caption:
If this sounds familiar, you're not lazy. You're depleted. 🧡

That's worth talking about with someone who'll listen without judging. Link in bio.
